gloss: no mistakes; a flawless performance (wasei-eigo from English "no" + "miss")

definitions.gloss: no mistakes; flawless execution (used in sports, exams, performances, and games where errors can be counted)
definitions.explanation: A Japanese-coined English compound meaning "performing without any mistakes" — a flawless run through a test, game, performance, sport, or task. It is commonly used in figure skating, gymnastics, music recitals, exam-results talk, and gaming/esports contexts, where a clean performance with zero errors is the goal. ノーミス is typically used as a predicate (with だ) or in the adverbial form ノーミスで ("without any mistakes").

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{試験|しけん}はノーミスだった。
examples.english: Today's exam was flawless (I made no mistakes).

examples.japanese: ノーミスで{演技|えんぎ}を{終|お}える。
examples.english: To finish a performance without any mistakes.

examples.japanese: ノーミスでフリーを{滑|すべ}り{切|き}った{選手|せんしゅ}に{大|おお}{歓声|かんせい}が{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: The skater who got through her free skate without a single mistake received huge cheers.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{練習|れんしゅう}を{重|かさ}ねたおかげで、{本番|ほんばん}ではノーミスで{曲|きょく}を{弾|ひ}き{終|お}えることができた。
examples.english: Thanks to repeated practice, I was able to play through the piece without any mistakes during the actual performance.

notes:
ノーミス is a wasei-eigo (Japanese-coined English) noun meaning "no mistakes" or "a flawless performance." It is widely used in performance and sports contexts.

WASEI-EIGO STATUS:
- Components: English "no" + "miss"
- The full compound "no miss" is not idiomatic English; English speakers would say "flawless," "clean," "perfect," or "without any mistakes." ノーミス should not be back-translated literally as "no miss" when writing English.

TYPICAL CONTEXTS:
- Figure skating, gymnastics, diving — sports where errors are noted and deducted
- Music recitals — performing a piece without flubs
- Exam talk — finishing a test without careless mistakes
- Video games / rhythm games / esports — completing a level or song without errors (often abbreviated NM or ノーミス{達成|たっせい})
- Driving tests, certifications, demonstrations

GRAMMATICAL BEHAVIOR:
- Predicate: 〜はノーミスだった ("~ was flawless")
- Adverbial: ノーミスで〜 ("in a flawless manner / without any mistakes")
- Compound modifier: ノーミス{演技|えんぎ} ("a flawless performance"), ノーミス{達成|たっせい} ("achieving a no-miss run")

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ノーミスで{終|お}わる: to finish without a mistake
- ノーミスで{滑|すべ}り{切|き}る: to skate through without a mistake (figure skating)
- ノーミスで{弾|ひ}き{切|き}る: to play through without a mistake (music)
- ノーミスを{狙|ねら}う: to aim for a flawless run
- ノーミス{達成|たっせい}: achieving a no-miss run
- ノーミス{演技|えんぎ}: a flawless performance
- {完全|かんぜん}ノーミス: "completely flawless" — for emphasis

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- ケアレスミス: careless mistake — the negative counterpart, a typical thing one tries to avoid
- {完璧|かんぺき}: perfect, flawless (general adjective) — broader; can describe more than just lack of errors
- ミスなし: "no mistakes" (without the ノー prefix) — uses native Japanese {無|な}し; close in meaning
- {一発|いっぱつ}{合格|ごうかく}: passing on the first try — related notion of clean success
- パーフェクト: "perfect" (loanword) — broader; often used for perfect scores or runs
- ミスゼロ: "zero mistakes" (less common than ノーミス but used similarly)
- {完投|かんとう}: complete game (baseball) — different but related notion of finishing without error

USAGE NOTES:
- ノーミス implies measurable mistakes — there must be something one can count as a mistake. It is awkward for situations like a casual conversation where mistakes are not formally tracked.
- In strict English writing, prefer "flawless," "clean," or "without any mistakes" — not "no miss."
- Often heard in sports broadcasts: "ノーミスで{演技|えんぎ}を{滑|すべ}り{切|き}りました!" ("She skated through without a single mistake!").
